cohort: The study included 229,816 singleton liveborn infants insured by the provincial public drug insurance in Quebec, born between 1998 and 2015.
finding: Assisted vaginal delivery and emergency cesarean section were associated with an increased risk of ADHD in children, compared with unassisted vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Assisted vaginal delivery and emergency cesarean section were associated with an increased risk of ADHD in children, compared with unassisted vaginal delivery.
